summary: The shell is built from restraint rules (white surfaces, hairlines, thin line glyphs, black bold type), which leaves all colour and character to small sticker-style icons drawn in four different dialects, while the brand's real character (warm photographs, orange and green, the handshake mark) appears only in the entry and then vanishes: Home is the entry's two roles (requester, worker) rendered as unframed clip-art with no button affordance. Navigation states are cuts and the hierarchy is flat or inverted: the tab switch, the loading skeleton and the arrival of content have no motion, the selected tab is a #F3F3F3 capsule on white (1.1:1), tile titles, section headings and card titles are all bold ink at 20/18/20 px, and the urgent 'Čeka te' list is drawn quieter than the less urgent next-Dogovor card. Meaning is overloaded: the same sheet-plus-orange-badge metaphor stands for 'publish' and 'my tasks', the same speech bubble for applications, Dogovori and chat, and green stands for primary action, selection, money and an unconfirmed term alike, so screens read as unclear even where the content is right.

findings.title: One icon language: distinct metaphor per concept, all drawn in the FactArt construction
findings.evidence: base_home.png: the 'Objavi zadatak' art (white sheet + orange badge with a plus) and the 'Moji zadaci' row icon (white clipboard + orange badge with a check) are near-twins on one screen but lead to different places; in the Zadaci ellipsis menu 'Objavi zadatak' even reuses the clipboard kind (DiscoveryPresentation.tsx:1234 icon 'tasks'). Speech-bubble silhouettes mean three different things: 'offers' (Moje prijave row, AttentionRow APPLICATION), 'agreements' (the Dogovori tab, AttentionRow AGREEMENT) and 'chat' (FactArt.tsx). The tab 'Zadaci' is a map while 'Moji zadaci' is a clipboard. Four drawing dialects on one screen: FactArt (3-tone edge/face/shine stickers), HomeLaunchArt (flat strokes), HomeIllustration (gradient hero), Phosphor thin outline glyphs in chrome (User, Bell, CaretRight, ArrowLeft). Owner reading of 'ikonice nose tekst': icons are not self-explaining and icon-only controls (profile glyph, bell, ellipsis, sliders, calendar) need the words next to them.
findings.problem: Icons neither identify their concept at a glance nor look like one family, so they work as decoration, not as navigation; this is a likely root of 'loše ikonice' and 'nejasni ekrani'.
findings.fix: Write the concept-to-icon table once (a comment block in FactArt.tsx plus a test) and draw each concept with its own silhouette: Početna = house (keep); Zadaci/browse = map (keep); Objavi zadatak = NEW 'publish' (sheet with a pencil or plus, green-led) used by the Home door, the Zadaci menu and any 'new task' action; Moji zadaci = clipboard 'tasks' (keep, only for the owner's own list); Prijava = NEW 'send' (paper plane); Dogovor = NEW 'handshake', the silhouette of the brand mark itself, replacing bubble+check on the tab and in lists; Poruke = the chat bubble only. Redraw HomeLaunchArt from FactArt's construction (ground shadow, edge 1.5 units under the face, shine, white details) so it is FactArt at 64-72 px, not a fourth style; keep HomeIllustration (the HOME signature) untouched. Chrome glyphs: Phosphor stays for controls (rule), but raise ChromeIconButton to weight 'bold' or 'duotone' at 22 px so they are not thinner than the art next to them, and give icon-only controls that are primary (filters, calendar) a visible word.
findings.risk: Three new drawings must hold at 16 px (task cards use 16) as well as 72 px; 'agreements' is used in many lists and notifications, so the swap cascades visually; the fact-art and pictogram tests enumerate kinds; icons stay aria-hidden with words beside them; orange tone list ORANGE_KINDS must be updated for the new kinds; no new package.
findings.verifyOnPhone: Each new icon at 16, 24, 32 and 72 px on the HONOR; the tab bar at selected and unselected state; Home rows 'Moji zadaci' vs the publish door side by side; check that no two different destinations on one screen share a silhouette.

findings.title: Tab bar: strong selected state with motion, icons that do not look disabled, no instant cut
findings.evidence: base_home.png, w5_zadaci.png, new_dogovori_aktivni.png: the selected tab is a #F3F3F3 capsule on a white bar (sys.color.greenSoft, about 1.1:1) so selection rests on icon and label colour only; inactive icons use FactArt's MUTED tone (#8A938E / #5C6860) which reads as greyed-out clip-art. Code (src/app/(app)/_layout.tsx): the capsule is a plain backgroundColor swap on the Press (lines 192-193), the tab navigator is `animation: 'none'` (line 180) so a tab switch is a hard cut and the capsule jumps; no tabBarBadge anywhere (grep), so nothing on the bar says that something waits for the person. Labels are the 12/16 'label' variant while the icons are ambiguous (see HP-02).
findings.problem: The one control that is on screen in every root has no motion, a barely visible selection and no signal; it feels static and template-like and does not reliably tell 'where you are' at a glance.
findings.fix: (1) Replace the backgroundColor swap by an absolutely-filled capsule child driven by a Reanimated shared value: withTiming(selected, sys.motion.toggle 180 ms, easeOut) on opacity and scaleX 0.9 to 1 (or one shared sliding capsule using measured tab x), plus a 20x3 green indicator pill on the capsule's top edge as the bar's one brand mark; icon wrapper does one 1.0 to 1.08 to 1 pop on select with sys.motion.spring; reduced motion (useReducedMotion) = instant. (2) Add a second MUTED tone for inactive tab art that keeps the two-tone colour at lower saturation instead of grey, and keep non-text contrast at 3:1 or better. (3) Labels use the existing `tab` variant (14/20, 600) instead of 12/16 700 with letterSpacing overridden to 0; the label height is already measured (rememberLabelHeight) so the bar height follows. (4) Optional: a fade scene transition (`animation: 'fade'`, about 120 ms) if the Zadaci map mount does not flash; optional attention dot only if fed by an existing server-owned read (Home's attention count), never invented.
findings.risk: The tab contract tests, the label-measurement and roomyLabels flex weights (LABEL_SPACE), 48 dp targets, accessibilityRole 'tab' and selected state, and Press's own 0.97 scale stacking with the capsule animation (avoid double motion); a scene fade could flash the map on first visit; at font scale 1.3 the bar must not grow.
findings.verifyOnPhone: Switch Početna, Zadaci, Dogovori repeatedly (screen recording): the capsule and icon move, no flash on the Zadaci map; reduced-motion on = instant; 320 dp and font 1.3 (labels, height); selected state readable outdoors-brightness; re-tapping the active tab still works.

findings.title: Home motion: breathing, shaped skeleton, gliding layout, one arrival; no hard cut
findings.evidence: Code: HomePresentation.tsx Skeleton (lines 144-146) is two static grey 64 px blocks, unlike every other screen's breathing, shape-matched SkeletonList (Skeleton.tsx 114-118, Arrive.tsx useBreath); after the read the sections simply appear and push 'Moji zadaci / Moje prijave' down (no layout animation exists anywhere in src: grep for LinearTransition/layout= finds none); Appear deliberately skips the first list (Appear.tsx useAppear), so a cold open has zero arrival; the root Stack is remounted by key on sign-in (src/app/_layout.tsx:126) with auth animation 'none', so the step from the entry or sign-in to Home is a hard cut. Judged from code, not seen in motion.
findings.problem: The first seconds of the app, after the carefully animated entry, are static and jumpy; this probably is a large part of 'loše animacije'.
findings.fix: (1) Replace Home's Skeleton with a SkeletonList-based placeholder shaped like the real blocks (an appointment-card shape plus two slim row shapes) and sized to the loaded height, so arrival is a cross-fade, not a jump. (2) Wrap the sections and the 'Moje' rows in Animated.View with Reanimated layout={LinearTransition.duration(sys.motion.enter)} so rows glide when a section above lands (container motion only, which the rule allows; reduced motion = no layout animation). (3) One arrival on a fresh Home mount (Home is keyed by user and accountRevision, so it plays after sign-in, not on tab returns): the two doors rise with Appear index 0 and 1 (FadeInDown, 40 ms stagger) or, with the illustrated fallback, the existing Arrive on the art; facts never animate. (4) Pull-to-refresh and the bell swing stay as they are.
findings.risk: Reanimated layout transitions inside a ScrollView with RefreshControl can stutter if overused (limit to the three containers); jest mocks of reanimated; the existing comment 'the tiles never move' guards against layout shift, so the arrival must be opacity/translate only and must not delay tappability.
findings.verifyOnPhone: Screen recording of cold start to Home on the HONOR over a slow network: skeleton breathes, no jump when sections land, doors arrive once and not again on tab return; reduced motion on = no motion; check no jank while the reads complete.

findings.title: The floating tab bar reserves its own band instead of floating over content
findings.evidence: All tab screenshots: the bar is a rounded pill with a shadow sitting in a band of white with nothing behind it; code: tabBarStyle height max(70, ...) + marginTop 8 + marginBottom max(12, inset), not absolute (src/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:196-200), so scene content ends above it. On base_home.png 'Moje prijave' is below the fold behind the bar's band; new_dogovori_aktivni.png has a large empty area above it.

Pick (b) first if the Zadaci docked list sheet geometry is not worth risking.

summary: The Zadaci screen is built from correct, carefully guarded parts that were never designed as one composition: a tall text-only card is the only unit of the list, the top bar crams a search pill, an X, a sliders icon and a "..." menu into one pill, and the map and the list behave like two screens joined by a button. At the owner's actual phone (361 dp wide) the card, the filter pill and several other components fall on different sides of ad-hoc width breakpoints (<340, <360, <375, <380, <390), so he permanently sees the "large text" stacked layouts, not the compact ones the design was made for, which is why everything looks big, repetitive (green title plus green price plus orange/green icons on every card) and unclear. Motion, icons and states each have a sound token system but are applied inconsistently (binary switches at the ends of springs, unanimated chip fold, FactArt micro-detail that is mud at 16-20 dp, a skeleton that does not match the real card, identical logo discs as map pins), so the biggest wins are a recomposed card/peek on one layout-class rule, a de-crowded top bar, one filter language and a small set of motion/icon fixes in shared components.

findings.title: Recompose the TaskCard: the compact layout never shows on a 361 dp phone, and the stacked one is a 333 dp wall of green text
findings.evidence: w5_zadaci.png: the first card spans y=780..1635 of 2000 (about 333 dp, 43% of the screen; list viewport shows 1.15 cards, the first card starts at 39% of the screen height). Title (3 lines, green 20/700) and the price (2.000 RSD, also green 20/700) are stacked and the same weight/colour; then three icon rows (place, time, vehicle); then a hairline and a foot that holds only a lonely icon + '0/1'. new_mz_aktivni.png and new_mz_filtered_istorija.png show the same face: 'Tražim ponude' is a full-width green row of its own and the foot is empty except '0/1'. Code: TaskCard.tsx line 56 `large = useTextScale() >= 1.3 || width < 380`; the R16 receipt records the owner's phone as 361 dp, so large is always true and CardHead (TaskFace.tsx 174-183) always stacks, CardBriefFoot stacks, facts use lines=0 (never clamp).
findings.problem: The side-by-side title/price head, compact foot and the 'fraction' foot were designed for ordinary width, but every phone under 380 dp is forced into the accessibility-resilience layout, so the owner never sees the designed card. summary: The five screens share one recipe: a heavily outlined 24dp card, a green 20/700 title, one 24dp-slot sticker icon per fact row, and a 12px dot-and-word status that is the smallest thing on the card, so the answer the owner opens these lists for (what state is this in, what do I do next) is the least visible element and every card looks like every other. The icons are glossy two-tone stickers in four hues (orange calendar and people next to green pin and money) drawn at six different sizes, with one speech-bubble silhouette reused for offers, chat and agreements, and a bare "0/1" fraction that carries meaning with no word. Layout defects make screens unclear: the tab rows are cut mid-word, the Pregled state line breaks into a ragged right column, Nacrti shows a filter-reset empty state when no filter exists, History cards say nothing about the outcome, and the Kandidati compare screen is a grid of grey panels rather than a comparison; motion is only a press-shrink and a first-arrival fade, so every tab, sort and compare change is a hard cut.

summary: The app has a decent but thin motion vocabulary (press scale, list arrival, sheet springs, segmented slide) that is applied unevenly: the biggest moments of movement, going into a screen, coming back, and data arriving after a skeleton, are either a cut or an accident of the navigator defaults (push fades in from white on the library's easeInOut, Back is a hard cut, loaded lists and photos pop in). Feedback is also undifferentiated: a selection haptic and a scale fire on every touch-down, including the start of a scroll, and about ten literals (800 ms art, 520/700/1600 ms loops, a second sheet spring, six press-scale values) bypass the tokens, so nothing reads as one designed system. All of it must be fixed under the B22 constraint, which means fewer, longer-lived Reanimated views (settled rows currently carry a wrapper they do not use, the lift is copy-pasted three times, and the only `exiting` animation is on a floating pill), transform/opacity only, and one reduced-motion source.

findings.title: Screen transitions are asymmetric: push fades in from blank white, Back is a hard cut, easing is the library default, direction follows route order
findings.evidence: src/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:29-30 (PUSH_TRANSITION = 'shift', timing 280, no easing), :157-159, :180 (three root tabs and redirects 'animation: none'); the file's own comment (:22-28) says pushes used to feel like redrawing. Library behaviour read in node_modules/expo-router/build/react-navigation/bottom-tabs/views/BottomTabView.js:109-127 and :183-207 plus TransitionConfigs/SceneStyleInterpolators.js:21-38: every route animates with its OWN spec; a route whose animation is 'none' gets no scene style and is detached at once (activityState INACTIVE); progress sign is `index >= state.index ? 1 : -1` (route registration order, not push vs pop); 'shift' = opacity + translateX +-50; Animated.timing without `easing` is easeInOut. src/app/_layout.tsx:131 uses native slide_from_right for dogovor/[id], obavestenja, prijave, a second transition language. Stills w5_zadaci.png -> new_pregled.png / new_kandidati.png show only the end states; the transition itself is NOT visible in screenshots, so this is read from code and must be confirmed on a screen recording.
findings.problem: About 30 screens (task detail, candidates, profile family, publish review, chat) are pushed inside the tabs navigator. On push the tab you leave has animation 'none', so it disappears immediately and the new screen fades in from white while sliding 50 px, with a slow easeInOut start. On Back the revealed tab is opaque, on top (zIndex 0) and instant, so the leaving screen's exit is hidden under it: a cut. Because direction follows registration order, a screen registered before the one you are on enters from the left. Three other screens slide natively. There is no continuity, which reads as redrawing instead of going somewhere (and as unclear orientation).
findings.fix: Stage 1 (S-M, no new package): (a) put the three roots on a short fade: Tabs.Screen index/zadaci/dogovori `animation: 'fade'` with transitionSpec {animation:'timing', config:{duration: sys.motion.tab (150), easing: Easing.bezier(...sys.motion.easeOut)}} so they take part in every transition and Back is no longer a cut, and tab-to-tab becomes a soft cross-fade; keep REDIRECT screens and reduced motion at 'none'. (b) Replace 'shift' on FULL screens with ONE custom `sceneStyleInterpolator` (supported option, BottomTabView.js:175) that ignores the sign of progress: opacity [-1,0,1]->[0,1,0] and translateY [16,0,16], duration sys.motion.push lowered to 240, easing easeOut passed explicitly in transitionSpec.config (the default easeInOut violates the app's own 'UI never eases in' token rule). Put the interpolator and spec in a new src/ui/system/transitions.ts and add `tab: 150`, `push: 240` to sys.motion. (c) Update the two contract tests that pin the old values (tabLayoutSafeAreaContract.test.ts:69-74 'instant peer tabs', v5-tab-navigation.test.tsx:151) deliberately. Stage 2 (L, only if the owner wants the real Android slide and predictive back, app.json has predictiveBackGestureEnabled false): move the pushed detail/flow screens under the root Stack where dogovor/[id] already lives; the custom tab history router (_layout.tsx:60-123) makes this a large, risky change, so do not start it before Stage 1 is judged on the phone.
findings.risk: During the 150-240 ms transition both screens stay attached (MaybeScreen keeps the leaving one active), so pushing from Zadaci keeps MapLibre plus the gorhom sheet rendering under the fade: possible jank and more Reanimated churn exactly where B22 is worst. The two contract tests intentionally change. Router history logic (retired routes, REPLACE-as-jump, FLOW_BEHIND) is not touched but must be re-run (retired-discovery-routes.test). Reduced motion must still give animation 'none' on every route.

findings.title: Data arrival has no motion: skeleton swaps to content in one frame, photos pop in from a spinner, lists never animate the first time they arrive
findings.evidence: src/ui/system/Appear.tsx:28-36 `settle` baselines the FIRST non-empty list as 'already there', which is right for a warm return but also swallows the first list that arrives AFTER a loading skeleton (Zadaci empty = StateView loading at DiscoveryPresentation.tsx:1040-1042, same hook in Moji zadaci, Dogovori, Moje prijave, Kandidati). src/ui/media/AuthorizedPhoto.tsx:76-78 `transition={0}` and :93 ActivityIndicator inside the well; the same file is used for 40-56 px portraits. new_dogovori_aktivni.png shows a stray spinner arc inside the 56 px portrait well beside the card; new_kandidati.png shows monogram avatars standing in. 24 files use ActivityIndicator for loading, 34 use the skeleton, so the loading language is mixed.
findings.problem: What the person experiences is: skeleton breathing, then a hard swap. A photo or portrait appears as a native Android spinner and then a pop. The rule in tokens.ts ('what moves is the container that carries it') is right, but the app applies it only to later-arriving rows, never to the main arrival, so screens feel unfinished and generic.
findings.fix: (1) Appear: add an optional third argument to useAppear().settle(keys, viewKey, {afterLoading}) so that the first non-empty list after a loading phase is an ARRIVAL (stagger sys.motion.stagger 40 ms, cap 6 rows, FadeInDown enter 240) while a cached or warm-return list stays still (EX-03c must not replay); the screens already know `loading`. (2) Add a screen-level `Arrive`-style wrapper: when StateView loading is replaced by content, fade the content container once, opacity only, 160 ms, ONE animated view per screen. (3) AuthorizedPhoto: `transition={{ duration: sys.motion.toggle, effect: 'cross-dissolve' }}` (expo-image, native, no new package) and for wells under 64 px draw the still sys.color.wash instead of an ActivityIndicator. (4) Rule: spinner only inside a button (V2Action loading) or a sub-second sub-element; a screen or a list loads with the skeleton; a photo well loads with the still wash.
findings.risk: Existing guard: no false arrival replay after filters, warm return and EX-03 local-first must stay still (src/ui/system/__tests__/appear.test.tsx, discovery-presentation, list-rows-memoized tests). More entering animations means more Reanimated views, so the 6-row cap and M5 budget apply. A cross-dissolve on an authorized photo must not delay the existing abort-on-unmount.
findings.verifyOnPhone: Cold open each list on a throttled connection: skeleton -> content must show a staggered 240 ms arrival of at most 6 rows; warm return and filter change must stay still (no replay). Count Reanimated animated views before/after via the B22 log counts (M1/M2) and gfxinfo janky % during the arrival; photo cross-dissolve 180 ms without a flash of the grey well.

findings.title: Press feedback and haptics are one undifferentiated touch-down tick: scale and haptic fire when a scroll starts, and outcomes (success, error) are silent
findings.evidence: src/ui/Press.tsx:84-98 fires scale and `fire(haptic)` in onPressIn; no `unstable_pressDelay` or delayPressIn exists anywhere in src (grep 0 hits) and RN Pressability defaults delayPressIn to 0 (node_modules/react-native/Libraries/Pressability/Pressability.js:462). About 103 call sites use haptic 'select', including pure navigation: TaskCard.tsx:92,108, HomePresentation.tsx:55,71,93,115, ScreenChrome.tsx:65 (back/close), DiscoveryPeek.tsx:71,138, CandidateFace.tsx:167,207. 'success'/'error' haptics are only reachable through SuccessMark.tsx:27 (V2Action's confirmed check and error line fire nothing). Press-scale values in use: 0.94, 0.97, 0.98, 0.986, 0.99 and 1 (grep scaleTo).
findings.problem: Putting a finger on a card to scroll the list ticks the phone and shrinks the card (then it springs back when the scroll takes the gesture): every list reads as jittery, and because every tap gets the same tick the haptic says nothing. Real outcomes (offer sent, Dogovor made, error) have no tactile answer. Six scale values give no scale hierarchy.
findings.fix: Rule: haptic = outcome, not touch. In Press add `hapticOn?: 'in' | 'release'` (default 'release' = inside onPress); keep 'in' only for state toggles where the tick IS the change (Segmented, chips, radio/checkbox rows, tab bar, switches). Set haptic='none' on pure navigation (ScreenChrome back/close, TaskCard/CandidateFace/Home rows/Peek rows). Map: select = a state changed; light = the one primary action committed; success/error = a server-confirmed result (V2Action `success` and `error` props, SuccessMark already). Shrink the scale ladder to three constants in sys.motion.pressScale: button 0.97, row/card 0.985, none (large surfaces); replace 0.94/0.98/0.986/0.99 in the ~45 sites and in CARD_PRESS_SCALE. Optional: for scrolling rows keep the scale at touch-down (it is cancelled by pressOut) but only start it after 60 ms (`unstable_pressDelay: 60`) so a flick never shows a shrink.
findings.risk: A mechanical sweep over ~100 sites: tests assert haptic wiring (press-reduced-motion.test, action-states.test); release haptics arrive about 80-130 ms after touch (minPressDuration 130 ms) which is right for navigation but must not be used for toggles; a delayed press-in must not make quick taps look dead (keep 60 ms or less).
screens: every screen (Press is the touch surface of the app)

TaskCard.tsx:84-90 adds a second Animated.View (lift) and its two Press children (scaleTo={1}, lines 92 and 108) each still create AnimatedPressable + useAnimatedStyle + a withTiming/withSpring on press (Press.tsx:72-100). DiscoveryListSheet.tsx:11-20 flips borderTopLeft/RightRadius 28 -> 0, borderWidth and boxShadow in one step when animatedIndex >= SNAP.full - 0.001, which a critically damped spring (SHEET_SPRING stiffness 300, damping 30) reaches only at its very end, so the rounded edge and shadow pop off after the sheet has visually stopped. DiscoverySearchBar.tsx:82 mounts/unmounts the chip row (U blizini / Na daljinu / Na licu mesta, visible in w5_zadaci.png) when `chipsShown` flips on scroll, which also changes toolsBottom and thereby the snap points.

findings.title: Rules and tokens: about ten motion literals bypass sys.motion, there are two sheet springs and a second animation engine; write down the rules and guard them
findings.evidence: Literals outside tokens: Arrive.tsx:16 (800 ms, own bezier) and :36-37 (700 ms), AiConversationShell.tsx:336 (520/140 ms), VoiceComposer.tsx:294 (1600 ms), SuccessMark.tsx:32 (spring damping 13 / stiffness 240), ProductSheet.tsx:20 SHEET_SPRING (stiffness 300, damping 30) beside sys.motion.springSheet (tokens.ts:189), Press.tsx spring {400, 0.85} versus card 0.986 (TaskCard.tsx:19). Two engines: RN Animated (8 components) and Reanimated 4.5.1 (Press, Appear, sheets, typing dots). The existing guard src/ui/system/__tests__/one-token-source.test.ts covers colours/type, not motion.
findings.problem: Nothing tells a developer which value to use, so every screen picks its own and the app feels like many small animations, not one product.
findings.fix: RULES (put in tokens.ts as the doc comment and in DESIGN_SKILLS.md): R1 Only transform and opacity move; never height, width, top or SVG props (BrandScene's locked entry excepted). R2 Enter decelerates (easeOut) and is longer than exit: enter 240, exit 160, push 240, tab 150, toggle 180, press 120 in / 400 spring out; every React Navigation or Animated.timing spec passes the easing explicitly. R3 Sheets and anything the finger carries use ONE critically damped spring (sys.motion.sheetSpring = stiffness 300, damping 30, overshootClamping); no overshoot on anything that carries text. R4 B22 rule: mounted-forever views; no `exiting` layout animation anywhere; a row's animated wrapper is decided at mount and never switches; at most 2 Reanimated views per list row; an `entering` only for a genuinely new id, capped at 6 rows; loops (skeleton breath, typing dots, glow) only on the focused screen, stopped in background and under reduced motion, never more than 4 at once. R5 Haptics are outcomes, not touches (M4). R6 Warm = still, cold-after-skeleton = arrive once, photos cross-dissolve 180 ms, spinner only inside a button (M3). R7 One reduced-motion source (ui/system/motion.ts): movement off, state change instant, Lottie on first frame, navigation 'none'. R8 Scale ladder: 0.97 button, 0.985 row/card, none for big surfaces. Put the missing values into sys.motion: tab 150, fade 160, sheetSpring, arrive 800 (named as a 'moment' tier), loop {breath 700, typing 520, glow 1600}; delete springSheet. Extend one-token-source.test.ts to fail on `duration:` numeric literals, `scaleTo={0.9x}` and `damping:` outside tokens.ts (allow the locked ENTRY_V49 and camera duration 0).

findings.title: Human chat messages snap in and the thread jumps to the end; the AI chat fades them in: two behaviours for one conversation pattern
findings.evidence: src/ui/AgreementChat.tsx:262-272 followLatest() calls scrollToEnd({animated:false}) synchronously and again on the next frame; :378-403 a plain ScrollView with all messages and no entering animation. AiConversationShell.tsx:348-354 gives every fresh turn FadeInDown 240 ms with an 8 px rise and tracks arrival by durable id (`arrival.shouldEnter`). Chat is not in the supplied screenshots: judged from code only.
findings.problem: In the Dogovor chat a sent or received message appears with a content jump and no cue of where it came from, while the AI conversation feels soft; the two feel like different products.
findings.fix: Reuse the AI shell's idea in a shared `MessageArrive` (RN Animated native driver, opacity 0 -> 1, translateY 6 -> 0, 160 ms, easeOut): animate only a message whose id was not displayed before (the same durable-id set the chat already keeps for reportDisplayed) and only when the thread is following the end; loaded history, restore and local-message replacement stay still (existing rule). In followLatest use scrollToEnd({animated: !reduced && deltaFromEnd <= viewportHeight}) for follow-ups after the first layout; the initial restore stays animated:false.

findings.verifyOnPhone: Two-device or fixture chat: send and receive 10 messages with the keyboard open and closed: each new message rises 6 px and fades in 160 ms, the thread follows only if already at the end, no jump when scrolled up, history load and restore show no motion. gfxinfo janky % while typing/sending <= 5 %.

summary: The Dogovor area is built correctly (guards, recovery, honest states) but drawn as three unrelated surfaces: a flat rule-separated list, a long form-like Pregled, and a chat with almost no visual or motion language of its own. The root of "generic / unclear / poor icons / poor motion" is systemic: two icon languages (glossy multi-layer FactArt plus thin Phosphor outlines) share every screen, one Dogovor is drawn three different ways with different role wording (list, Početna, calendar), and the conversation, the main activity of a Dogovor, is hidden behind an unlabeled icon while rare actions fill the page as full-width rows. Motion exists only as press scale and new-row fade; everything else (pane swaps, state changes, disclosure bodies, message arrival, success moments) is an instant swap, and voice messages have working plumbing but no UI slot yet, so the composer should be redesigned once, for text, photo and voice together.

summary: The app has no single icon system: it has five drawing dialects (2.5D two-tone FactArt, gradient Pictogram, flat HomeLaunchArt, glossy off-palette Catalog27 PNGs on three deep screens, thin Phosphor lines) plus six hand-built status dots, with the same idea (map, star, send, lock, support) drawn two to four ways and 47 line glyphs used at ten different sizes. The colour illustrations the owner wants to keep are drawn for 32 px and above but sit at 14 to 20 px in every card row, where pale ground shadows, white-on-white bodies, a per-kind orange/green split that breaks the repo's own one-orange-accent rule, ticks drawn inside calendars and one speech-bubble silhouette used for three meanings make them read as decoration that the words beside them have to explain; meanwhile the real controls (search, filters, calendar) are bare glyphs that squeeze the words next to them. findings.title: Adopt ONE icon strategy: one family, three registers, one rulebook (FactArt stays, no new package)
findings.evidence: Inventory read from code: FactArt 27 kinds (~135 call sites, 55 files, sizes 14/16/18/20/24/26/28/30/32/36/56); Pictogram 46 kinds (pickers, 40-56 px); HomeLaunchArt 2 (flat, token colours, grey hairline); CatalogArt 4 glossy PNGs (yellow padlock, blue-white lifebuoy, grey sheet, blue shield: assets/catalog27/*.png); Phosphor 47 distinct glyphs in 63 files at 13/14/16/18/20/21/22/24/28/40 px; six separate hand-built status dots. Same concept drawn several ways: map = FactArt map in the tab bar (w5_zadaci, new_dogovori_aktivni), HomeLaunchArt 'discover' tile (base_home), Phosphor MapTrifold on the 'Mapa' pill (w5_zadaci), FactArt map again as the empty-state picture (new_mz_nacrti); star = FactArt star 14 px (new_kandidati) vs Phosphor Star 28/40 (AgreementReviewPresentation.tsx:89,112); send = PaperPlaneTilt fill 20 (PillComposer.tsx:53) vs ArrowUp bold 22 (AiConversationShell.tsx:292). base_home alone shows three dialects at once: HomeLaunchArt tiles, FactArt house/map/bubble tabs, Phosphor line profile and bell.
findings.problem: The owner's 'generic, poor icons' is not one bad icon; it is the absence of rules. Each layer was added by a different round (V28 transcription, picker pictograms, Home R13 art, Catalog27, Phosphor), so no screen looks like it was drawn by one hand. AGENTS 3.6.4 already says FactArt is the one icon system for facts and line icons are for controls only, but nothing enforces sizes, tones, weights or which family draws what. FactArt should stay (the owner's colour art, 'do not replace with an all-gray generic set', design-diagnosis-20260925/REPORT.md); what must change is how it is cut for small sizes, coloured, and kept unambiguous (see ICO-02 to ICO-04).
findings.fix:
Strategy: ONE FAMILY, THREE REGISTERS.
(1) FactArt = what a thing IS (facts, destinations, row subjects, empty/success art). Keep all 27 kinds. New API in src/ui/system/FactArt.tsx: <FactArt kind={FactArtKind} size?: FactSize /*16|20|24|32|48|64, default 20*/ tone?: 'brand'|'accent'|'quiet'|'danger' /*default 'brand'*/ cut?: 'auto'|'mark'|'art' /*auto: size<=24 -> mark, else art*/ muted?: boolean /*deprecated alias of tone='quiet' so the 12+ muted call sites and SettingsRow auto-mute keep working*/ />.
(2) Glyph (new src/ui/system/Glyph.tsx) = what you DO (back, close, caret, plus, minus, check, send, search, filters, more, mic, wave, arrows). Wraps Phosphor: <Glyph name={GlyphName} size?: 16|20|24 tone?: 'ink'|'green'|'muted'|'onGreen'|'danger' on?: boolean />; weight is decided inside (bold for size<=16 and for check/close/plus/minus, regular at 20+, fill only for on). Closed registry of ~26 names. ChromeIconButton keeps accepting a Phosphor `icon` for back-compat and also accepts a GlyphName.
(3) StatusMark (new src/ui/system/StatusMark.tsx) = where a thing stands: <StatusMark state='open'|'done'|'waiting'|'closed'|'alert' size?: 14|16 /> (shape plus tone, never colour alone). Pictogram stays for pickers only (>=32 px, unchanged). BrandMark/BrandLockup, entry assets, mascot, map-pin brand mark: untouched.
Rules in one file docs/implementation/design-system/ICON_SYSTEM.md plus three guard tests: no 'phosphor-react-native' import outside Glyph.tsx (allow-list the existing files during migration, shrink it per phase); FactArt/Glyph sizes typed to the ladder; no hand-built 6-8 px status dots.
MIGRATION ORDER (coherent batches, one APK per two phases, per AGENTS 3.2.3): P0 owner decisions + A/B sheet on dizajn-tabla (ICO-03 tone, ICO-10 Catalog27); P1 FactArt mark cut + tone + ladder (ICO-02, ICO-03: every card row changes at once); P2 meaning fixes + StatusMark (ICO-04, ICO-07); P3 Glyph + chrome words + tab bar (ICO-05, ICO-06, ICO-08); P4 moments, CatalogArt retirement, map unification (ICO-09 to ICO-12). KEEP: brand mascot/entry/HOME signature, BrandMark map pins, Pictogram pickers, FactArt art-cut drawings at 28+ px, orange star in ratings, the bell swing, SuccessMark fresh/haptic boundary.
BEFORE/AFTER the phone should show: on every list card (new_mz_aktivni, new_mp_sve, w5_zadaci) the fact rows are one hue, equal weight, no grey smudge under the icon; orange appears only on counts, unread dots, urgent and waiting; at most three icon sizes and one stroke weight per screen; tab icons crisp when inactive; primary controls carry a word; no orphan separator dots.

Tests that assert drawing details (src/ui/system/__tests__/fact-art.test.tsx, task-card-face, application-face, candidate-face, inbox-native, state-view) and the phosphor Proxy mock (__mocks__/phosphor-react-native.js renders host elements named after the glyph, screen-chrome.test imports named glyphs) must keep passing: keep `icon: Icon` and `muted` accepted. 63 files import Phosphor, so migrate the system components first (about 80 percent of what is visible) and let the guard test's allow-list shrink.

findings.title: Give FactArt a flat 'mark' cut for 24 px and below (today the 2.5D art is used at 16-20 px in every card row)
findings.evidence: FactArt.tsx header: the drawings are built as ground-shadow ellipse + darker edge 1.5 units under the face + light shine + white/pale details on a 32-unit canvas, and the call sites put them at 16 px (ApplicationFace.tsx:138-166, CandidateFace.tsx:179, TaskFace.tsx:223,275) and 20 px (TaskCard.tsx:97-99, DiscoveryPeek.tsx:75-76, AgreementCollectionPresentation.tsx:148-159). In the screenshots the secondary shapes disappear or turn to mush: the calendar is a white body with a 1.1-unit pale outline on a white card with a tick and two ticks-for-lines inside (new_mp_sve, base_prijave_now); the users icon is an orange person plus a near-invisible pale 'ghost' person (new_mz_aktivni '0/1', new_pregled '1/2'); the banknote reads as a green rectangle with a '0' (new_mp_sve 'Tvoja ponuda'); the tiny van is the only one that survives (w5_zadaci). Sizes judged by eye from the screenshots, not measured.
findings.problem: Detail that works at 32-64 px is below the legibility floor at 16-20 px: the light/soft tones (#D6DAD6, #FFF0E2, #E1F4EC) are under 3:1 on white and the 0.5-1 px edges and shines add noise, so the icon becomes a coloured smudge. It then explains nothing and the words carry the row, which is the 'icons are poor / icons need text' feeling. The repo already half-admits this: vehicle and tool were drawn separately 'because the picker pictogram turned to mush at 16 px' (TaskFace.tsx:76).
findings.fix: In src/ui/system/FactArt.tsx add the cut. `drawing(kind, tone, muted)` already builds every kind from three closures (shadow, edge(), shine()), so the first pass is cheap: add a `flat` flag; when flat, shadow is null, edge() and shine() return null, and line() uses width >= 2.4 units. Then hand-fix the kinds whose raw underlay shapes bypass those helpers (users, person, check, info, support, star, shield, lock, eye, money, photo use raw `c.edge` circles/rects offset by 1-1.5 units: convert them to flat-aware). Mark-cut construction rules (32-grid): one fill tone + one white inner detail; no element lighter than 3:1 on white (drop `soft`/`light` shapes; both people in 'users' get the full tone, back one smaller); minimum stroke 2.4 units (1.2 dp at 16), minimum gap 3 units; at most 3 shapes. Per-kind simplifications for the busiest: calendar = outlined body + filled header band + two ring ticks + two lines (no checkbox, no tick); tasks = clipboard + two lines (no badge); money = one banknote + circle; clock = circle + two hands; support = ring; pin = solid + white dot. Auto-select by size (size <= 24 -> mark, >= 28 -> art) so the ~135 call sites need no edit, and keep the existing art cut for Profile rows (26), Home rows (32), StateView (56), picker use. Update the size ladder (FactSize) so 14/18/26/28/30/36 stop appearing (14 -> 16, 18 -> 20, 26/28/30 -> 24 or 32, 36 -> 32).
findings.risk: fact-art.test.tsx asserts the ground shadow (ry 1.6, cy 29.4) at 16 px for vehicle/tool and 'no orange'; it must be rewritten to assert the cut per size and a contrast floor, not deleted. Several presentation tests find FactArt by kind and size. About 19 of the 27 kinds are used at <= 24 px, so the per-kind hand fixes are the real cost (2-3 days); the helper-nulling pass alone is under a day and already removes most of the smudge. TaskCard/Peek visual freeze is lifted by the owner, so card rows may change.

findings.title: One tone rule: green by default, orange only for attention, and bind the art greens to the UI green
findings.evidence: FactArt.tsx:28 hard-codes ORANGE_KINDS = calendar, users, bell, tasks, person, star, support, so in every card the rows alternate hue by kind: green pin, orange calendar, green van, orange users, green banknote (new_mz_aktivni, new_mp_sve, w5_zadaci). The repo's own rule says the opposite: tokens.ts and ScreenChrome.tsx 'critique B1: orange is the screen's one accent' and AGENTS 3.6.4 'orange stays an accent only (Home publish tile, what waits, map +)'. HomePresentation.tsx:75 even uses an orange dot as 'the one mark of attention' on a picture that may itself be orange (users/tasks kinds). Second mismatch: FactArt GREEN.front is #079C77 (a lighter emerald) while sys.color.green, the headings, the primary button and the active tab label are #076E4E; in base_home the pin and house read minty next to the deep-green title and button.
findings.problem: Colour in the icons is decoration, not information: the hue says nothing about the fact, orange is spent on every row so it can no longer mean 'this waits for you', and the lighter emerald against the deep brand green looks pasted in. This is a large part of 'generic clip-art' on every list screen.
findings.fix: Replace ORANGE_KINDS and the MUTED/ORANGE/GREEN consts with a tone prop: 'brand' (default, all kinds), 'accent' (orange, only where something needs attention: unread, waiting for you, urgent, counts, the rating star), 'quiet' (replaces `muted`: inactive, disabled, historic), 'danger'. Derive the tones from tokens: add a `sys.color.art` group in tokens.ts (front = sys.color.green or a one-step lighter value chosen by A/B on the phone, edge = greenEdge, light/soft derived) so FactArt no longer owns hex values. In the art cut the second hue may remain as a small detail (calendar ring, badge dot) so the owner's two-tone identity survives at 28+ px; in the mark cut a row is single-tone. Keep orange explicitly on: HomePresentation attention dot, TaskFace/CandidateFace rating star, inbox unread dot, urgent badge. Call sites that set `muted` keep working through the alias.
findings.risk: Owner-visible palette change: the 2026-09-22 'identičan izgled' decision drew time and people in orange; the later R12 (2026-09-25) and B1 direction and the owner's 2026-10-02 complaint supersede it, but show him an A/B first. Tests that assert 'no orange' or colour lists (fact-art.test, pictogram.test) change. The raw-hex guard (one-token-source.test.ts) does not cover FactArt today; adding FactArt to COLOUR_SCOPE is the point. Pictogram keeps its own tones for pickers; align its green too.

findings.title: Fix icon meaning collisions: ticks that mean 'not confirmed', one bubble for three ideas, one clipboard for four events
findings.evidence: FactArt.tsx: calendar draws a tick inside (line 47), tasks carries an orange check badge (line 81), remote draws a tick on its screen (line 65), agreements/shield/check also tick. Yet the calendar is the picture of 'Termin nije potvrđen' (base_home appointment card, new_dogovori_aktivni) and 'Fleksibilan termin' (base_prijave_zavrsene), so an unconfirmed appointment carries a confirmation tick; the clipboard-with-check is the row for 'Pomoć pri nošenju ormara, 1 od 2 mesta je slobodno' (new_kandidati) and 'Moji zadaci, 2 aktivna' (base_home). One speech-bubble silhouette is used for Dogovori (tab, agreements), 'Tražim ponude' price mode (offers; new_mz_aktivni, new_mz_istorija, new_pregled) and a message note (chat; base_prijave_zavrsene 'Ugiggig'). InboxPresentation.tsx:80-92 maps four different events (new task, revised, cancelled, opportunities) to 'tasks' and both COMPLETION_REQUIRED and 'execution' to 'check'; 'info' is used for a requirement condition (TaskFace.tsx:81), the About row (ProfileHubPresentation.tsx:108) and as the default error/offline picture (StateView.tsx:14). 'Nema zadataka u ovom prikazu' (a filtered-empty list) is drawn with the map (MarketplacePresentation.tsx:141, new_mz_nacrti).
findings.problem: An icon whose silhouette or detail can mean several things teaches the person to ignore it, so the words must do all the work ('icons carry text'). Worse, a tick says 'done/confirmed' where the fact is the opposite.
findings.fix: (a) Add a meaning table next to the kinds in FactArt.tsx: `FACT_MEANING: Record<FactArtKind, string>` (one phrase per kind) and a unit test that no two kinds share a meaning phrase, so the table stays honest. (b) Redraw: remove the tick from calendar, tasks and remote (in both cuts); keep ticks only on check, agreements (agreed) and shield if the owner wants it. (c) 'offers' (price mode 'Tražim ponude') becomes a price tag (distinct silhouette); 'chat' stays the bubble with three dots; 'agreements' (tab) stays bubble plus check; so the three bubbles stop being one. findings.title: One Glyph wrapper for the 47 Phosphor control icons: three sizes, one weight rule, one colour rule
findings.evidence: Scan: 47 distinct Phosphor glyphs in 63 files at 10 sizes (13, 14, 16, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24, 28, 40), weights regular/bold/fill chosen per site. In one bar (w5_zadaci) the magnifier is green 20, the sliders ink 22 regular, the X bold 16, '···' ink 22. Sibling Home rows use different chevrons: attention row ink 18 (HomePresentation.tsx:83), 'Moji zadaci' row muted 18 (:122), appointment card green 20 (:96); base_home shows the green one next to the grey ones. A search glyph is 21 px in MarketplacePresentation.tsx:160 and 20 px in DiscoverySearchBar.tsx:90. Two send glyphs (PillComposer.tsx:53, AiConversationShell.tsx:292). The thin regular-weight chrome glyphs (back arrow, sliders, '···' in new_pregled, new_mz_aktivni) are visibly lighter than the 600-700 Inter titles beside them.
findings.problem: Controls are individually fine and collectively unregulated, so every screen's top bar and every list row has slightly different glyph weight, size and colour. That is the 'looks like a template assembled from parts' feeling for the line-icon layer.
findings.fix: Create src/ui/system/Glyph.tsx with a closed GlyphName registry mapped to Phosphor components (~26 names: back, close, caret-right/down/up/left, plus, minus, check, send, search, filters, more, mic, wave, arrow-right, arrow-up, arrow-up-right, refresh, trash, camera, image, eye, eye-off, external, expand, info, map). Props: size 16|20|24 (chrome = 24, row/inline = 20, in-text = 16; kill 13/14/18/21/22/28/40), tone ink|green|muted|onGreen|danger (chevrons are muted everywhere unless the whole row is the green action), weight resolved inside (bold at <= 16 and for check/close/plus/minus, regular at 20+, fill only for on-states). Migrate in this order: ScreenChrome (chrome.icon 22 -> 24), V2Action and Press icons, DiscoverySearchBar, MarketplacePresentation, HomePresentation, SettingsPresentation, Disclosure, PillComposer and AiConversationShell (one send glyph), then the long tail. Add the jest import guard with a shrinking allow-list. Try bold at 20 for chrome glyphs on the phone before locking (the owner asked for stronger, not larger, type).
findings.risk: The phosphor Proxy mock renders host elements named after the glyph and several tests import named glyphs and assert them (screen-chrome.test.tsx, action-states.test.tsx, pkg011-slice4-presentation.test.tsx): Glyph must render the Phosphor component for the mapped name so those assertions hold. Changing chrome.icon from 22 to 24 touches the 48/44 px geometry the chrome tests pin. Keep the zero-new-package rule: Phosphor is already installed and used (phosphor-react-native ^3.0.6), including its duotone weight if wanted later.
findings.verifyOnPhone: Photograph the root bar, a detail bar, a flow bar and the AI composer before/after: glyph sizes read as three steps, strokes match the title weight, chevrons one colour per row type.

findings.title: Give empty, error and success moments a deliberate picture (and draw the success tick) instead of one clipboard and a pale check

(b) SuccessMark: render the FactArt check art cut and draw the tick on with a stroke-dash animation (react-native-svg + Reanimated animatedProps, about 220 ms) only when `fresh`; keep the existing haptic and the reduced-motion path (static final frame); animation completion must call nothing. (c) Lottie: do not ship Catalog27 (glossy, off-palette). Leave LottieArt as is until the owner supplies files in the product palette, then use them for 'Dogovoreno!' and the first empty state only. No new package.

findings.title: Trust line: one star drawing, aligned to the first text line, and one idiom for the same facts

Icon sizes and legibility were judged by eye from 1264x2728 screenshots; I did not measure rendered pixel sizes or contrast, and I could not render the proposed mark cut (read-only, no build). The A/B and the dizajn-tabla board (uskociapp://dizajn-tabla, internal build) were not opened.
